module_title: Norms, Standards, PTR, and School Management Committees (SMC)
introduction: This intermediate tier transitions into the hard data, mechanical norms, and infrastructural standards that the RTE Act 2009 imposes on schools. It details the highly tested Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) formulas, working hours, and the democratic composition of the School Management Committee (SMC).

core_concepts.title: Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) Norms
core_concepts.description:
RTE explicitly mandates the minimum number of teachers based on student enrollment.
Primary Level (Class 1 to 5):
- General PTR is **1:30**.
- If student enrollment exceeds 200, the PTR becomes **1:40** (excluding Head Teacher).
- A full-time Head Teacher is required if enrollment exceeds 150 students.
Upper Primary Level (Class 6 to 8):
- General PTR is **1:35**.
- A full-time Head Teacher is required if enrollment exceeds 100 students.
- Must have at least one teacher each for: Science & Math, Social Studies, and Languages.

core_concepts.title: Working Days and Instructional Hours
core_concepts.description:
RTE specifies the absolute minimum academic exposure a child must receive annually:
1. Minimum Working Days:
   - Primary (1-5): **200 days** per year.
   - Upper Primary (6-8): **220 days** per year.
2. Minimum Instructional Hours:
   - Primary (1-5): **800 hours** per year.
   - Upper Primary (6-8): **1000 hours** per year.
3. Teacher's Working Hours: A teacher must maintain a minimum of **45 working hours per week** (including preparation time).

core_concepts.title: School Management Committee (SMC) - Section 21
core_concepts.description:
To democratize education and ensure community participation, every government and aided school must form an SMC.
Composition Mandates:
- **75%** of the members MUST be parents or guardians of the students.
- **50%** of the total members MUST be women.
- Proportionate representation must be given to parents of children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups.
Role: To monitor school working, prepare the School Development Plan (SDP), and monitor the utilization of government grants.

core_concepts.title: 25% Reservation for Weaker Sections - Section 12(1)(c)
core_concepts.description: A landmark clause forcing inclusion. It mandates that all Private Unaided Schools must reserve at least **25% of their seats at the entry-level** (Class 1 or Pre-primary) for children belonging to Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and disadvantaged groups in the neighborhood, providing them free education. The government reimburses the school for these students.

important_entities.name: 45 Hours Per Week
important_entities.key_fact: The minimum weekly working hours for a teacher under RTE.
important_entities.significance: This is a guaranteed 1-mark question in almost every TET exam. Note that this 45-hour mandate explicitly includes BOTH teaching hours in the classroom AND preparation time at school.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Primary vs. Upper Primary PTR Confusion
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Students frequently mix up the ratios. 
- Primary (1-5) is 1:30. 
- Upper Primary (6-8) is 1:35. 
Why? Because upper primary students are older and slightly more independent, allowing a teacher to manage a slightly larger class size.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In any question regarding SMC structure, immediately look for the numbers 75% (for parents) and 50% (for women). If an option says '50% parents', it is definitively wrong.

exam_strategy_tips: If a math-based pedagogy question asks: 'A primary school has 125 students. According to RTE, how many teachers are required?', calculate using the 1:30 ratio. 125/30 = 4.16. Since you cannot have a fraction of a teacher, the school requires **5 teachers**.
